newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech rail unions end national strike.
newsitem.headline: Czech rail unions end national strike.

text.p: Czech rail unions agreed to end a five-day-old national strike from midnight (2300 GMT) on Saturday after marathon talks with government representatives, CTK news agency reported.
It said Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux announced the agreement after six hours of talks.
Jaromir Dusek, chairman of the Association of Unions of Railway Workers (OSZ), said: "A compromise was reached which will enable rail transport to recommence fully from midnight."

The strike, which began on Tuesday and was originally planned to last just 48 hours, was called to demand a rethink of government plans for reform of the rail system which could cost tens of thousands of jobs.
Under the compromise deal, the Transport Ministry agreed to come up with a new transport strategy by May 31. The rail unions would be consulted on the plans, CTK said.
The strike crippled the national rail network and businesses said it would have a serious impact on earnings if it continued much longer.
Unions representing power workers had threatened to stage sympathy stoppages if no agreement was reached.
The strike was the first major conflict between organised labour and the government since the fall of communism in 1989, but the threat of more public sector unrest remains.
Teachers are holding daily selective strikes forcing the closure of primary and secondary schools and there are persistent threats of stoppages by doctors and health-care workers.
